items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data into a new matrix by placing variables from different sources one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This approach could be tested to combine NIR and Raman spectra into a single augmented dataset, provided the sampling geometry and time steps are synchronized.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This reviewed concept may not directly apply to the customer's feed frame without proper block-scaling normalization and validation on independent batches, as literature notes that instrument complementarity does not always improve predictive performance.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
